Run a grid of parameter sets x seeds in parallel

Source: R/grid.R
run_grid.Rd

Runs every (parameter set, seed) cell, each in its own directory <set>_seed<seed> under outdir_base, in parallel with the current future plan. Set workers for a quick local multisession; for a cluster, set future::plan(...) yourself before calling and leave workers = NULL, so that the grid runs under your plan.

Usage

run_grid(
  param_sets,
  seeds = 1L,
  outdir_base,
  model = slim_model(),
  workers = NULL,
  verbose = NULL,
  skip_existing = TRUE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

param_sets

a vivax_params() object, or a list of them (or of lists of overrides). Its names name the cells' directories: they must differ, also ignoring case, and be usable as a directory name; blank names become set01, set02, ... by position.

seeds

whole-number seeds to run for each set, none repeated.

outdir_base

the grid's directory, created if needed.

model

path to the SLiM model.

workers

if set, run under future::plan(multisession, workers) for this call (the previous plan is restored afterward). Set it to the cores you can spare. If NULL, use the current plan.

verbose

passed to run_sim().

skip_existing

if TRUE (the default), a cell that already holds its run is not run again.

overwrite

if TRUE, a cell that holds another run, or one that did not finish, is run again and its run replaced once the new one has finished. Files that are not part of a run are never replaced.

...

passed to run_sim().

Value

a data.table with one row per cell, by set then seed: set, seed, outdir, ok (the cell holds its run, run now or before), skipped (it was not run again), error (the failure message, or NA), extinct_tick (the tick on which the run went extinct and ended, NA if it did not) and never_started (TRUE for a founder-free run whose imports never established a parasite; see load_run()), both NA for a failed cell, elapsed_s, finished (UTC), slim_version and malariafwd_version, from the run's DONE, and then one column per parameter whose value differs between the sets, of the parameter's type. A cell that never started is ok: not starting is an outcome of the grid, which never_started records. Its run holds no parasite, so its event and genetic summaries are empty or NA: keep the cells with ok & !never_started for those, and count the cells that never started as an outcome. The cells that went extinct, those that never started, and those not run again are counted in one message each. A failed cell does not abort the grid – its directory is left as it was and its files and log are in <cell>.failed – but it warns, and the reason travels with the result. A warning given in the cells (such as a parameter set's own warnings, which run_sim() repeats for each run) is given once, after the warning that lists the failed cells, with the number of cells it came from. If the grid stops part-way with an error, that error's message lists the warnings of the cells whose results had reached this session; with workers, a cell's warnings travel with its result. A cell whose worker dies is run again on a new worker, its first attempt's directory left beside it as <cell>.partial-...; if that worker dies too, the grid stops with an error that names the cell. Under options(warn = 2) a warning in a cell fails that cell, in any plan and also inside suppressWarnings(), and the warning that lists the failed cells is then an error, so nothing is returned; the cells that ran are on disk. The caller's random-number stream is left as it was.

Details

Every set is checked, and every cell's directory, before any cell starts: a set vivax_params() refuses, or a cell whose directory run_sim() would refuse, stops the grid with all of them listed. A cell that already holds its run (the same parameters, seed and model) is not run again, so calling run_grid() again with the same sets and seeds resumes a grid that stopped part-way, and adding seeds or sets runs only the new cells. The cells of an edited set hold another run and stop the grid unless overwrite = TRUE.

grid.tsv in outdir_base, written when the grid finishes (also when cells failed), records each cell: its outcome, versions, the key of its run and every parameter. load_grid() reads it. Cells run by other means, such as one run_sim() per job of a job array, are recorded by calling run_grid() with the same sets and seeds afterwards, which runs nothing. Two grids writing into one outdir_base at the same time race on grid.tsv; a later call rebuilds it.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # slim_available()
sets <- list(low = vivax_params(BITING_RATE = 0.05, SIM_DAYS = 100),
             high = vivax_params(BITING_RATE = 0.12, SIM_DAYS = 100))
out <- tempfile("sweep")
g <- run_grid(sets, seeds = 1:2, outdir_base = out)   # workers = 2 for two at a time
g
load_grid(out)
}
